purpose: Map the interaction between temporary underground disruption, insurgent regenerative rate, and capital exhaustion from a common live-insurgency anchor. Test whether pressure produces a double bind in which weak regeneration cannot replace underground losses while aggressive regeneration preserves stock at the cost of capital runway.
theory_basis: Fresh static assays show that partial underground thinning raises recruitment pressure when any one of several access channels survives.
Source accounting implies an unconstrained marginal equipment cost of 1.92 insurgent capital units per recruited represented person.
Prior independent mobilization confirmation established a high-recruitment metabolic ceiling: multiplier 0.25 collapsed 16/16 worlds from capital exhaustion, while 0.125 collapsed 4/16.
The current dynamic-confirmation run is independent of this phase-map contract; this phase map uses a new seed block.

design.model_semantics: Current implemented semantics remain frozen, including the documented disrupted_sympathy_retention mismatch.

primary_phase_outputs: rooted armed membership at day240 and day360
fielded force at day240 and day360
canonical insurgent capital at day240 and day360
cumulative recruited represented population since anchor
predeclared_contrasts: Within each recruitment multiplier, U-on minus U-off effects on rooted membership, capital, cumulative recruitment, recruitment hazard, footholds, and fielded force.
Within U-off and U-on separately, compare the three recruitment multipliers on final rooted membership, final capital, and cumulative recruitment.
Estimate the paired capital cost per excess recruited represented person wherever excess recruitment is nonzero.
Report canonical collapse/zero-capital fractions by cell without selecting a best strategy.
directional_predictions: Cumulative recruited represented population increases with post-anchor recruitment multiplier in the U-off cells.
The U-on rooted-membership effect at day240 is negative at all three tested recruitment multipliers.
The magnitude of the day240 rooted-membership deficit under U is larger at recruitment multiplier 0.03125 than at 0.0625 because replacement capacity is lower.
Where U induces positive excess recruitment, its paired capital effect is negative and approximately tracks the source-derived 1.92-unit marginal equipment cost until capital constraints bind.
exploratory_phase_questions: Does 0.125 recruitment absorb more underground loss but incur enough capital depletion to increase collapse risk?
Is there a middle regenerative band that best preserves both rooted stock and capital runway under pressure?
Does disruption move worlds toward the previously confirmed metabolic ceiling by inducing extra replacement flow?
stop_rule: Do not add more recruitment-rate cells to this seed block after outcomes. If the transition lies outside the frozen grid, expand on new seeds under a new contract.
guard: Synthetic mechanism phase map only; no real-world policy ranking or operational recommendation.
